meta.what_this_is: Ground truth for the sample bundles: for each one, the rule ids a correct run should produce, the ones it must not produce, and the behaviour expected of the gate. scripts/evaluate.py measures a real run against this file; tests/test_expectations.py checks the file itself stays in step with rules/legal_rules.json.
meta.what_it_proves_and_what_it_does_not: These bundles were written by the team to contain known clauses, so a score here measures whether the pipeline finds what was deliberately planted in documents shaped like the ones it targets. It is not a measurement against real contracts, and it cannot be: nobody on the team has a labelled set of real ones. Treat a number from this harness as a regression signal and as an upper bound on real-world recall, never as a claim about the tool's accuracy in the field. See ETHICS.md, risk 1.
meta.how_to_read_the_three_lists: expect_rules: the run is wrong if these do not fire - each corresponds to a clause deliberately written into the bundle. forbid_rules: the run is wrong if these do fire, which is how false positives are caught. watch_rules: reported but not scored, because whether they fire depends on arithmetic against figures that change (the minimum wage moves twice a year) or on a judgement the team has not settled.
meta.how_bundle_names_work: A bundle directory is named bundle_<letter>_<language>_<what it is>. The language code is the language the documents themselves are written in, not the language the report is produced in: it is in the name because what the pipeline has to read differs per language, and a run that scores well on the Dutch bundles proves nothing about the English ones. The nl bundles carry the clauses as Dutch agencies word them; the en bundles exist so that the same structures can be read, and a failure diagnosed, by someone who does not read Dutch.

bundle_a_nl_tied_housing.description: The case the tool exists for: three documents that are unremarkable individually and serious together.

clause_map.NL-WAADI-09-FEE: Art. 5: bemiddelingsvergoeding of EUR 350,00 charged to the worker and recovered by deduction.
clause_map.NL-WAADI-09A-OBSTRUCTION: Art. 8: EUR 2.500,00 payable if the worker takes a job directly with the hiring company.
clause_map.NL-ID-RETENTION: Identity document held for the duration of the contract.
clause_map.RS-TIED-HOUSING: Art. 7.1 housing supplied in connection with the placement, and art. 3 ends the contract with the assignment.
clause_map.RS-EVERYTHING-AT-ONCE: Art. 7: housing, transport (EUR 80,00 a month) and insurance (EUR 145,00 a month) all supplied by the agency and all ending together.
clause_map.RS-NO-HOURS-NO-OTHER-WORK: No guaranteed hours combined with a ban on working elsewhere - two clauses, one finding.
clause_map.RS-ADVANCE-PLUS-PENALTY: Art. 6: EUR 400,00 travel advance repaid at EUR 100,00 a month, alongside a penalty for leaving early.
clause_map.RS-ASYMMETRIC-NOTICE: Art. 3.3: one month's notice from the worker against two working days from the agency.
clause_map.RS-PENALTY-CLAUSES: EUR 150,00 per lost item, plus the early-departure penalty.
clause_map.RS-OPEN-ENDED-DEDUCTION: The machtiging covers named and unnamed obligations, is irrevocable, has no ceiling and no end date, and has the worker agree in advance to falling below the minimum wage.
clause_map.ET-WAADI-08-EQUAL-PAY: An uitzendovereenkomst, so the equal-treatment question applies.
clause_map.ET-EXPENSE-SWAP: Art. 4: EUR 2,10 of the EUR 13,50 hourly rate relabelled as verblijfkosten, stated in the contract itself not to count towards the wage.
clause_map.NL-WML-BELOW-MINIMUM: EUR 13,50 gross per hour is below the statutory EUR 14,99 before the expense relabelling and the deductions are considered at all.

watch_notes.NL-WML-13-DEDUCTION-CEILING: Settled on 2026-09-22 and still a watch rather than an expectation. The ceiling is 25% of the minimum wage the worker earns, which since 1 January 2024 is reckoned per hour worked: EUR 3.75 an hour at the 2026 figure of EUR 14.99, so about EUR 150 in a 40-hour week. The planted housing charge is EUR 112,50 a week, which is under that - and under it on a 36-hour reckoning too (EUR 134,91), so the choice the team was weighing does not decide this bundle either way; see docs/decisions.md. Whether the rule fires therefore depends on whether the check aggregates the other deductions with housing, which is a design question about the check and not about this bundle. It stays on watch so that a change in either direction is noticed rather than scored.

bundle_a_nl_tied_housing.cross_document_expectation: The employer and the landlord share an address and hold consecutive KvK numbers. This is visible only by reading two documents together and is what step 3 exists for; the harness does not score it because it is not a rule id, but a run that misses it should be noticed by whoever reads the report.

bundle_b_nl_clean.description: The control. A direct employment contract with guaranteed hours, symmetrical notice, housing independent of the job, no fees and no open-ended deductions.

watch_notes.NL-WML-BELOW-MINIMUM: Depends on the hourly figure in the contract against a minimum wage that moves every 1 January and 1 July. A control bundle that silently falls below the minimum after an indexation is worth knowing about, which is why it is watched rather than forbidden.

bundle_b_nl_clean.cross_document_expectation: This bundle is the false-positive check. It is also the check that a quiet result is reported as 'we did not find these problems in these documents' and never as a clean bill of health - that wording is asserted by tests/test_safety.py, not here.

bundle_c_nl_incomplete.description: One agency contract that charges for four things whose agreements were not supplied.

clause_map.ET-WAADI-08-EQUAL-PAY: An uitzendovereenkomst, so the equal-treatment question applies here as in bundle A.

watch_notes.RS-TIED-HOUSING: The contract deducts rent but the housing agreement is missing, so whether the tie can be established from what was supplied is exactly the judgement this bundle exists to exercise.

bundle_c_nl_incomplete.cross_document_expectation: The scored behaviour here is expect_missing_documents: the report must name the agreements the contract charges for but does not contain. Article 5.2 - a signed declaration that the worker received and read annexes nobody can produce - must not be treated as evidence that those annexes are unobjectionable.

bundle_d_nl_conflicting.description: A contract and an addendum signed the same day, contradicting each other on nearly every term that matters, each claiming precedence over the other.
bundle_d_nl_conflicting.cross_document_expectation: The scored behaviour is the gate. A run must come back gated with the conflicts listed, and must not present one of the two hourly rates as the worker's wage. Extraction here is easy and reads cleanly, so a gate that watched only the confidence score would sail past it: this bundle is the check that conflict gating is independent of confidence.

bundle_e_en_tied_housing.description: The English counterpart of bundle A: the same structures, worded as an agency's own English translation. Two documents - an agency contract and an accommodation annex from a company at the same address - that are survivable apart and serious together.

clause_map.NL-WAADI-09-FEE: Art. 5.1: a one-off placement fee of EUR 295,00 charged to the worker and settled by deduction from the first wage.
clause_map.NL-WAADI-09A-OBSTRUCTION: Art. 9.1: EUR 2.000,00 payable if the worker takes a job with the client company within twelve months.
clause_map.NL-ID-RETENTION: Art. 11.1: the identity document is kept in the agency's administration for the duration of the contract.
clause_map.RS-TIED-HOUSING: Annex art. 1.2 provides the bed space in connection with the placement; contract art. 3.2 ends the contract with the placement.
clause_map.RS-EVERYTHING-AT-ONCE: Art. 7: accommodation, transport (EUR 75,00 a month) and health insurance (EUR 150,00 a month) all arranged by the agency and all ending with the placement.
clause_map.RS-NO-HOURS-NO-OTHER-WORK: Art. 2.1 guarantees no hours; art. 8.1 forbids work for anyone else without written permission. Two clauses, one finding.
clause_map.RS-ADVANCE-PLUS-PENALTY: Art. 6: a EUR 375,00 travel advance repaid at EUR 95,00 a month, with the balance payable in full if the worker leaves within six months.
clause_map.RS-ASYMMETRIC-NOTICE: Art. 3.3 against art. 3.4: one month's notice from the worker, two working days from the agency.
clause_map.RS-PENALTY-CLAUSES: Art. 10.1: EUR 125,00 per lost item, deducted from the next wage, alongside the early-departure penalty in art. 6.3.
clause_map.RS-OPEN-ENDED-DEDUCTION: Annex art. 4: the authorisation covers named and unnamed amounts, is indefinite, cannot be revoked while anything is outstanding, has no ceiling, and has the occupant agree in advance to being paid below the minimum wage.
clause_map.ET-WAADI-08-EQUAL-PAY: An agency contract with the agency clause, so the equal-treatment question applies.
clause_map.ET-EXPENSE-SWAP: Art. 4.3: EUR 1,85 of the EUR 14,20 hourly rate relabelled as an untaxed living-expenses allowance, stated in the contract not to count towards the pension basis.
clause_map.NL-WML-BELOW-MINIMUM: EUR 14,20 gross per hour is below the statutory EUR 14,99 before the relabelling in art. 4.3 and the deductions are considered at all.

watch_notes.NL-WML-13-DEDUCTION-CEILING: Accommodation is EUR 118,00 a week against a 25% ceiling of roughly EUR 135 on a 36-hour reckoning, so the housing line alone sits under the ceiling and whether this fires depends on how the check treats the transport and insurance deductions together - the same open question as bundle A, and it is open for the same reason.

bundle_e_en_tied_housing.cross_document_expectation: Northfield Staffing Solutions and Northfield Housing Services share an address and hold consecutive Chamber of Commerce numbers, and the annex names the agency as the party doing the deducting. As in bundle A this is only visible by reading the two documents together and is not scored as a rule id, but a run that misses it should be noticed by whoever reads the report. The reason this bundle exists is that every clause above is planted in English: the four nl bundles cannot tell us whether a miss is a reading failure or a Dutch-language failure, and this one can.

bundle_f_en_clean.description: The English control. One direct employment contract with guaranteed hours, symmetrical notice, housing independent of the job, no fees, no relabelled pay and no open-ended deductions.

watch_notes.NL-WML-13-DEDUCTION-CEILING: Nothing is deducted here beyond what the law requires, so this should not fire; it is watched rather than forbidden because the check reads a figure that moves twice a year and a future indexation is a better thing to be told about than to be failed by.
watch_notes.RS-PENALTY-CLAUSES: Art. 8.1 says explicitly that no costs are charged for loss or damage. The rule keys on any penalty money term, so this is watched as the place a false positive on that rule would show up first.

bundle_f_en_clean.cross_document_expectation: The false-positive check, in English. NL-WML-BELOW-MINIMUM is forbidden here rather than watched because EUR 16,80 sits well clear of the statutory figure. This bundle is also the one that shows an English run producing a quiet result honestly: it must come back as 'we did not find these specific problems in the documents you gave us', never as a clean bill of health.
